title: Claude Output Watermarking & the EU AI Act
content:
## Overview

Starting August 11, 2026, Anthropic announced that Claude embeds **machine-readable watermarks** into its output by default — worldwide, not only for users in the EU. The change is Anthropic's response to Article 50 of the EU AI Act, whose AI-generated-content transparency obligations became legally enforceable on August 2, 2026.

---

## What Gets Watermarked

The marking method differs by output type:

- **Text:** an imperceptible, machine-readable watermark embedded directly in generated text. It doesn't change how the text reads to a human, but it can be detected programmatically.
- **Images (.svg, .png, .jpg):** signed **C2PA provenance metadata** — the same content-provenance standard used elsewhere in the industry — is attached to image output. Anthropic is explicit that this is provenance signaling, not a forensic guarantee: detection of the C2PA metadata is not conclusive proof of AI generation, since metadata can be stripped by downstream tools.

---

## Which Models Are Covered

- Any Claude model **released on or after August 2, 2026** ships with watermarking enabled at launch — this includes Claude Opus 5.
- Earlier models (the Claude 4.x line, Sonnet 5, Fable 5 if released before the cutoff) are being **retrofitted** rather than shipping the capability at initial release.

---

## Where It Applies

Anthropic rolled the watermarking out across its entire surface area, not just claude.ai:

- Claude.ai (consumer product)
- Claude Platform / API
- Claude Code
- Claude Cowork
- Claude Tag (Claude in Slack)
- Cloud partner platforms: AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry

The deliberate choice to apply this **globally** rather than gating it to EU traffic mirrors a pattern seen with other EU-driven compliance rules (e.g., GDPR-style features rolling out worldwide): it's simpler to run one code path than to maintain region-specific behavior, and it gets ahead of similar transparency rules likely to appear in other jurisdictions.

---

## Legal Context: EU AI Act Article 50

Article 50 of the EU AI Act imposes transparency obligations on providers of AI systems that generate synthetic text, audio, image, or video content — requiring outputs to be marked in a machine-readable format so they can be identified as AI-generated. Anthropic committed to the Act's **Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content**, a voluntary compliance mechanism that regulators treat as a safe harbor for the underlying legal requirement.

Non-compliance with the AI Act's transparency provisions can trigger fines of up to **€15 million or 3% of global annual turnover**, whichever is higher.

---

## Practical Notes for Developers

- The watermark is not visible in normal use — it does not add stray characters or alter formatting in API responses or Claude Code output.
- There is no API flag to disable it as of this writing; it is on by default for covered models.
- Because detection tooling for the text watermark is not yet public, developers can't currently verify programmatically whether a given piece of text carries Anthropic's mark — the mechanism is designed for use by Anthropic and authorized verifiers, not general-purpose detection.
